preStudy.title: Pre-Study: Check Your Readiness
preStudy.subtitle: Review essential prerequisite concepts: simplifying fractions, ratio equivalence, and rates before studying proportion.

cards.title: 1. Simplifying Fractions to Lowest Terms
cards.desc:
Divide the numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor (GCD):
• $\frac{12}{18} = \frac{12 \div 6}{18 \div 6} = \frac{2}{3}$
• Ratios with identical irreducible fractions represent equivalent quantities.

cards.title: 2. Understanding Ratios & Rates
cards.desc:
A ratio compares quantities of the same unit, while a rate compares different units:
• Ratio: $\frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}$
• Rate: $\frac{8\text{ eggs}}{2\text{ cups}} = \frac{4\text{ eggs}}{1\text{ cup}}$

cards.title: 3. Cross-Multiplication Principle
cards.desc:
If two fractions are equal $\frac{a}{b} = \frac{c}{d}$, their cross products are equal:
$$a \times d = b \times c$$ If $\frac{3}{4} = \frac{6}{8}$, then $3 \times 8 = 4 \times 6 = 24$.

foundation.formulaSubtext: A proportion is an equality of at least two ratios or two rates. For four quantities $a, b, c, d$ in proportion, the product of extremes equals the product of means.

rules.title: Concept of Proportion
rules.desc: A proportion is an equality of at least two ratios or two rates.

rules.title: Writing Proportion
rules.desc: If quantities $a, b, c, d$ are proportional, then $\frac{a}{b} = \frac{c}{d}$. $a, d$ are Extremes; $b, c$ are Means.

rules.title: Cross Multiplication Property
rules.desc: Product of Extremes = Product of Means: $a \times d = b \times c$.

rules.title: Solving Proportion Definition
rules.desc: Solving the proportion means finding the unknown value in the proportion.

ideas.flashcardTitle: Idea 1: Testing Proportions via Cross Products & Simplification
ideas.flashcardText: If the product of extremes equals the product of means ($ad = bc$), then the pair of ratios represents a proportion.

cards.q:
Determine whether the pair represents a proportion:
$$\frac{3}{8} \quad \text{and} \quad \frac{6}{10}$$
cards.ans: $\frac{3}{8}$ and $\frac{6}{10}$ do NOT represent a proportion.

ideas.flashcardTitle: Idea 4: Graphical Representation of Proportion & The Origin Test
ideas.flashcardText: Points must lie on a straight line passing through $(0, 0)$.

cards.tag: Solved Example 4.1 • Distance vs Time Tables
cards.q:
Determine graphically whether distance is proportional to time:
Table 1: Time (1, 2, 3, 4), Distance (70, 140, 210, 280)
Table 2: Time (1, 2, 3, 4), Distance (80, 100, 190, 260)

steps.text: Table 1: Points lie on a straight line through $(0, 0) \implies$ Proportional.
Table 2: Points do NOT lie on a straight line $\implies$ Not proportional.

cards.ans: Table 1 is proportional; Table 2 is not proportional.

cards.tag: Solved Example 4.2 • Origin Line Test Analysis
cards.q: Which of the relationships shown represents a proportion? (a) Curve through (0,0) (b) Straight line through origin (0,0) to (8,8) (c) Straight line through (0,1) (d) Straight line through (0,4)

steps.text: Graph (b) is a straight line passing through $(0, 0)$.

cards.tag: Solved Example 4.3 • Travel vs Delivery Costs
cards.q:
Determine which table shows a proportional relationship:
1) Covered distances [6, 12, 18, 24] m in [1, 2, 3, 4] s.
2) Price of pies with delivery [25, 45, 65, 85] LE.

steps.text: Table 1 has constant ratio 6 m/s through $(0,0) \implies$ Proportional.
Table 2 has 5 LE delivery fee at zero pies ($y = 20x + 5$) $\implies$ Not proportional.

cards.ans: Table 1 is proportional; Table 2 is not proportional.

2) Shampoo: [40, 50, 58, 70] LE for [100, 200, 300, 400] mL.

steps.text: Apples ratio is constant ($45\text{ LE/kg}$) through $(0,0) \implies$ Proportional.
Shampoo ratios are not constant $\implies$ Not proportional.

cards.ans: Apples is proportional; Shampoo is not proportional.
